body: 1. #Trincomalee Trincomalee which belongs to the Eastern Province of Sri Lanka considered as a bit hot area. It is popular for its own natural harbor. Main nation who live there is Tamil community. Main tourist attraction in this area is the coastal sandy beach. Uppaweli, Marble beach, #Nilaweli_beach, #Arisimale beach and Trinco beach are the most beautiful beach areas that I can recommend personally. Many foreigners who are in love with Sri Lankan climate visit the coastal areas to chill in the sun shines. Sun and sea is so closed with many tourists as it is #so Sri Lanka. Even you can do watersports like Diving, Scuba diving, snorkeling definitely in Trinco area. It’s unbelievable to see the hot water springs in Trinco. Have you ever seen or heard about this water springs that I’m saying about? It always springs out hot water from these natural wells. Also you can bath there and get the real experience of what I said. I think that you cannot have a proper idea about what I said till you see the place which I said.So can you at least imagine on this? “What is called this hot water spring” If not let’s have a visit there and enjoy our day time with this unbelievable place. Koneshwaram temple (or we called it as a Kovil) is a main religious place where people visit without any religious margin.People from all over the country visit this place without any religious difference. They pray for god and plead mercy from god on their troubles which they face in their lives.Though this is especially important for the Tamil community in Sri Lanka other people also visit this place and they have various myths and believes made around this place.This is a place where full within the whole year from local and foreign visitors. This is situated a bit far away from the main road but crowded a lot.Though the area is crowded a lot still the wild deer are working here and there beside the roads to this big Kovil, because they have already practiced to be fed from the visitors. “Welgam vehera” a ruined temple which reveals so many details about an ancient civilization of our Sri Lanka.Buddhist people who visit Trinco area never forget to visit this ancient temple. You will feel very calm nature after visiting the place. Those are the highlights which I can bring towards you about the Trincomalee area. Anyway my invitation is for all of you to experience this beautiful sun and sea.

body: The Trincomalee beach is one of the most beautiful and exotic I have ever seen. And I have traveled a lot in my life (35 countries, including Peru, India, Majorka and Ibiza...). Hotels need a lot to answer to this standard and, as everywhere in Sri Lanka tourist industry workers need a lot of work and education. Activities are quite good, e.g. dolphin watching (not a must) and exceptional, e.g. Pigeon Island snorkeling ( a must). We were not very lucky to see black rock sharks (not dangerous, they say they eat only fish) and/or a turtle, but my experience of looking at all those exotic fish and filming them under water was incredible, unbelievable, so a MUST. We were a family group of 4 without children or teens, but I tick friends in the next paragraph, since I don't have the choice I need. The entrance to the beach is free, the activities a bit expensive. Photos are from our dolphin watching and Pigeon Island snorkeling.

body: I visited Sri Lanka in June 2011. It was hot as the rains were delayed that year. I was with a friend and we set out for Trincomalee from Kandy by bus. It was a small, airconditioned bus. The trip took about four hours, passing through ares devastated by the recently concluded war. We set out early in the morning - after a lip-smacking breakfast of iddiappam and coffee - and by the time we reached our destination the sun was at its zenith and we were frying. We managed to get a room - cooled by a noisy fan - close to the beach. And what a beach! After freshening up, we straightaway made for the beach. What we saw delighted us. Just swathes and swathes of white sand and not a soul around. We plunged into the sea. We struck up an acquaintance with a life guard - called Leonard - who regaled us with diving stories. We had lunch at the only large resort on that beach - relaxing on their hammocks, sun-bathing and sea bathing. We stayed there the whole day practically. I would definitely recommend this beach as a must-visit in Sri Lanka. For those interested in diving, there are plenty of opportunities from a nearby island.

title: things to check before visiting
body: When specifying different places you want to see, be sure to get the guide to confirm that what you want to see is available that time of the season. For example, my guide told me that we could go to Trincomalee and take the boat to snorkel on a Wednesday. I found out just before Wednesday that boat trips to see whales/dolphins in Trincomalee is only available by Navy ships on Sat and Sun and only if they have at least 100 passengers. Also, if the waves are too high, then no boats will be allowed to go out for safety reasons. I was told that no small or private ships are allowed in Trincomalee. Also, for example, in September 2012, the road from Sigiriya to Trincomalee has a lot of construction, so the drive will be long (~3.5 hrs) and parts of it will be stop and go due to one way traffic allowed at one time. So, if you *really* want to go somewhere, make sure the driver is clear about what you want or he might talk you into somewhere else once you are in Sri Lanka, like my driver Siroshan Silva did. He committed to going and then backed out. It turned out on that day in my itinerary, which I very clearly indicated on email, that attraction was not available and he didn't check that before telling me that it was possible. I do not recommend him. The rating is based on other ratings and I didn't want to throw off the average. I'm just trying to provide info, so people can plan their trip, if they want to take the boat trip.

body: We went to Trinco with Ranuka in July when we heard that it is the best time of year to visit north-western Sri Lanka. Our guide was really helpful in putting together our itinerary on the go as we did not have any in mind when we arrived. We visited Fort Frederick as well as went on a scuba diving tour. The drive back from Trino to Colombo was a bit long but again our guide brought us to the Hot Springs and the ancient site of Mihinthale. We highly recommend our guide! title: Sea Shells!!!
body: I have visited almost every beach in Sri Lanka. This is the best out of the lot in terms of cleanliness. The beach is especially clean in the Nilaveli area and Marble Beach area. One of the other special things about the beach is that there is a lot of sea shells everywhere. Various kinds! Sometimes while picking up the shells, you may pick up a live one or two as well. Watch out for that. In the Uppuveli area, in one part of the beach we found a couple of dead Puff Fishes. Probably they have fallen off fishing nets. You might also want to be mindful of jelly fish as people say that there are more jelly fish in the sea in this area. We did see some sea urchins in China Bay but not in Nilaveli or Uppuveli. But on one occasion, we saw a couple of tiny creatures of different shapes and they looked like plastic. As regards the sea, there is a tendency for the sea in this area to get rough in different parts of the year. Although the sea was not too rough at the time we visited, we were advised neither to swim in the sea nor to go to Pigeon Island as it might be dangerous. There are indications of the condition of the sea near all the hotels so I guess one does not have to worry too much in that regard. If you are white skinned and if you want a tan in a clean beach, this is THE place for that!
